Tech Report: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2833 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

Recent findings suggest that AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

Industry observers note that united’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

Recent findings suggest that more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Major chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

Recent findings suggest that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

In a recent development, manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by newly introduced signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

According to recent reports, manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

In a recent development, united have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

Sources indicate that A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

In a recent development, estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

According to recent reports, milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

In a recent development, the players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely latest cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

In a recent development, carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE.

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his latest role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

In a recent development, “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

It has been revealed that “Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

Industry observers note that welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

According to recent reports, at the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri remarked Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Industry observers note that carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

In a recent development, kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Axalta (AXTA +2.33%) declared that its gross debt fell below $3 billion for the first time in the organization's history. Financial discipline and steady cash generation give the business room to navigate market headwinds while funding key growth initiatives. Three things management mentioned stand out.

Cutting overall debt directly reduces annual interest expense and protects profitability during economic slowdowns. Lower leverage gives the company additional flexibility as it prepares for its proposed combination with AkzoNobel.

Winning multishop operators (large body shop chains) expands customer coverage even when overall repair volume stays soft. Upfront investments to onboard these shops trade near-term margins for reliable multiyear revenue.

Combining operations creates significant scale advantages and eliminates duplicate corporate overhead. Anticipated cost savings bolster long-term operating efficiency while opening cross-selling channels across global markets.

Sources indicate that commercial vehicle demand and customer conversions are building momentum across core markets. High customer retention and consistent profitability (measured as adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or EBITDA) support future value, while management focuses on raw material inflation and pricing discipline.

Integration planning for the proposed merger continues to advance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 25, 2026 at 8:43PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Cognizant Technology Solutions ›.

It has been revealed that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Cognizant (CTSH +3.84%) unveiled constant-currency revenue growth of 4.8% year over year to $5.7 billion. Expanding profit margins and rising revenue per associate demonstrate that the adoption of software automation is enhancing operational efficiency across enterprise consulting operations. Three key takeaways from management's comments highlight how this transformation affects long-term shareholder value.

Cognizant is shifting client agreements from traditional billable hours toward outcome-based pricing, which ties fees directly to delivered operational results rather than billable hours. This commercial evolution enables the IT services provider to capture higher margins as software automation handles an increasing share of client workflows.

Specialized offerings in business process outsourcing (BPO), cybersecurity, infrastructure, and industry-specific software are expanding faster than standard consulting units. These artificial intelligence-assisted business segments generate roughly 40% of total company sales while providing a distinct growth buffer against macroeconomic headwinds in healthcare and retail sectors.

Recent findings suggest that management reduced its total projected outlay for Project Leap, a corporate restructuring program designed to optimize operational costs, because internal retraining programs successfully reallocated existing staff. By reskilling employees into artificial intelligence roles rather than paying severance, Cognizant preserves capital while upgrading workforce capabilities.

    #119574. Industry News: Is Nvidia Stock a Buy After Dell's Record AI Backlog?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (856 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Is Nvidia Stock a Buy After Dell's Record AI Backlog?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dell Technologies (DELL +0.60%) has a record $132.3 billion in artificial intelligence (AI) server orders it hasn't shipped yet.
    • It has been revealed that the report came after a tough day for Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) shareholders.
    • Dell builds full AI server racks, many of them around Nvidia's chips.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 25, 2026 at 9:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Dell Technologies (DELL +0.60%) has a record $132.3 billion in artificial intelligence (AI) server orders it hasn't shipped yet. The server maker reported that backlog with its fiscal third-quarter results after the market closed on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Three months before, the total was $95 billion.

    It has been revealed that the report came after a tough day for Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) shareholders. Nvidia's shares lost almost 6% on Nov. 24, giving back some of a 31% gain the day before, when the company said its board had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. They closed around $155, about 35% under the $239.24 record close they set on Oct. 6. Dell's results came out after the bell, so none of that drop was a response to them.

    Dell builds full AI server racks, many of them around Nvidia's chips. That makes its order book one of the more useful outside checks on demand for Nvidia's hardware. And I think it suggests that demand is still growing.

    Recent findings suggest that in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, which ended Oct. 30, 2026, Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders, while its AI server revenue grew 291% year over year to a record $22 billion. With orders coming in at almost three times the rate of shipments, the backlog kept climbing. It's now over seven times the $18.4 billion Dell posted a year before. At the third quarter's shipping pace, it covers around six quarters of AI server revenue.

    Orders slipped a bit from the fiscal second quarter's record $60.9 billion, so the record this time was in the backlog. But it was still Dell's second straight quarter with over $60 billion of AI orders. Dell also lifted its full-year forecast for AI server revenue to $78 billion, up from the $74 billion it expected three months before.

    Dell doesn't break out how much of its backlog is built on Nvidia's chips. It also sells servers based on Advanced Micro Devices hardware, so not every dollar belongs to Nvidia.

    "The proof point is our orders momentum, $180 billion over the past four quarters, with a majority of our new orders based on Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72," noted Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and chief operating officer, in his prepared remarks for the earnings call.

    Recent findings suggest that vera Rubin NVL72 is a full rack of Nvidia's latest AI hardware, and Nvidia started shipping it in its fiscal 2027 third quarter, which ended Oct. 25, 2026. So most of Dell's latest orders are for the product Nvidia is ramping up right now.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's revenue from AI clouds, industrial companies, and enterprises hit $47.5 billion that quarter. That almost tripled from $16.1 billion a year before and climbed 18% from the previous quarter.

    According to recent reports, on Nvidia's Nov. 17 earnings call, Colette Kress, the organization's chief financial officer, credited some of the sequential growth to Vera Rubin shipments to top neoclouds (specialized cloud companies that rent out AI computing power). Dell counts neoclouds among its AI server customers, too, along with governments and other businesses.

    On the same call, Kress raised Nvidia's forecast for revenue growth in fiscal 2028 (which ends in January 2028) to around 75%, from 70%.

    The share price doesn't seem to show much of that confidence. At around $142 on the morning of Nov. 25, after another drop of about 8%, Nvidia's stock costs around 8.5 times earnings, using analysts' average estimate for fiscal 2028. For comparison, FactSet put the forward price-to-earnings ratio of the S&P 500 at around 17 as of Nov. 20, based on expected earnings for the next 12 months.

    Put another way, investors are paying about half the S&P 500's forward price-to-earnings multiple for a tech giant forecasting 75% growth. Some of that discount might still come from Huang's Nov. 11 resignation and the uncertainty it caused. But it also suggests many investors doubt the growth will last.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    A backlog isn't revenue yet, of course. Customers need financing and data centers with enough power before Dell can deliver, so Dell says it screens every order for access to capital, land, and power.

    "We've had no customers reschedule business," Clarke said on the call, answering an analyst.

    Is Dell's record backlog enough reason to buy Nvidia stock?

    Not by itself. But Dell's numbers, along with Nvidia's raised forecast for fiscal 2028, point to demand for Nvidia's latest systems that's still rising, even with the stock well below its October record. At this price, I'd consider buying the stock.

    Recent findings suggest that we're onto Week 6! Here is the 9-cat version of my risers and fallers list. These rankings are for rest-of-season 9-cat leagues, and I'm leaning on Yahoo's rankings from the last two weeks and last month. Efficiency matters more here than in points leagues, and it's the main thing separating these six players. Let's get into it!

    Industry observers note that ausar is averaging 10.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.6 steals and 1 block on 55% shooting through 16 games, and he's been even better lately. He's eighth over the last two weeks and 30th over the last month. He leads the Pistons in rebounding and had a 17-board game against Philadelphia on Nov. 4. The weak spots are well known. Those with punt-3 builds get the most out of him, since he positively adds value in rebounds, assists, stocks and field goal percentage. The jump to 73% from the line is another win, as he doesn't hurt you nearly as badly as he used to.

    I have him 57th, as I anticipate Jalen Duren's return will impact his numbers to some degree. Either way, he's exceeding expectations in what could be a breakout campaign.

    Smith is averaging 14.1 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.1 3s and 1 block in 25.3 minutes, shooting 55% from the field with 0.9 turnovers per game. That mix of 3s, blocks, field goal percentage and low turnovers is why he grades out well in 9-cat without much volume. He's 14th over the last two weeks and 26th over the last month. He was drafted in just 8% of Yahoo leagues, so if you scooped him up off waivers, you're playing with house money.

    I'm moving him up to 65th, from 99th, but not higher because much of this production came with Nic Claxton sidelined. Caleb Wilson is also out, and Claxton is still ramping up, so Smith's role should hold for now. I could be too low on him. Continue to hold.

    McDaniels is 11th over the last two weeks and 18th over the last month. The bump in usage comes from Anthony Edwards' absence. Edwards is out until late January after knee surgery, and McDaniels has absorbed a bigger share of the offense without losing efficiency. He's averaging 18.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.2 steals, 0.9 blocks and 1.6 3s in 33.9 minutes, shooting 56% from the field and 85% from the line.

    According to recent reports, he's positive in eight of nine categories, with turnovers (2.2 per game) the only negative. I don't value turnovers that much, especially when he's so productive across other areas of fantasy. Some of that scoring should come back down when Edwards returns, which is why I have him 30th, up from 43rd. I wouldn't sell, even though his play is on another level right now.

    Hart is 233rd over the last two weeks and 176th over the last month. His scoring is down to 6.6 points per game from 12.0 last season, and he's shooting 34% from the field and 60% from the line. He's still contributing 6.7 rebounds and 4.0 assists, which keeps him rosterable, but his steals have dipped recently and he's listed as questionable with a right shoulder sprain. In 9-cat, the low percentages make it a bigger problem. The good news is that his minutes appear to be trending back up. Landry Shamet's been eating into his minutes because of his shooting, but over the past two games, Hart's averaging 37 minutes per gam. He's also coming off a 10-11-10 triple-double, which could be a nice selling point if you're concerned about his ROS outlook.

    I have him 120th, down from 72nd. I'd hold in 12-team 9-cat leagues for now since his shooting should improve, but he's not as bad as Mikal Bridges, who was near drop status.

    Sources indicate that gobert is 239th over the last two weeks and 289th over the last month. His rebound and block rates are both down: he's averaging 10.6 rebounds and 1.0 block in 29.2 minutes, compared to 11.5 and 1.6 last season. His scoring has dropped from 10.9 to 7.6 points, and his field goal percentage is down to 49% after he shot 68.2% last season. That FG% was the main reason to roster him in 9-cat. He's also shooting 46% from the line on 4.7 attempts per game. That's way too much volume for someone shooting so poorly.

    The former four-time defensive player of the year is more of a rebound specialist, so I'd look to move him if he can string together a few big double-double outings. I have him 150th, down from 110th. I'm probably still too generous.

    Reid has the volume in his first season in Charlotte: 17.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.5 3s in 31.5 minutes. The problem is efficiency. He's shooting 38% from the field on 17.5 attempts and 66% from the line, well below his career norms (45.6% and 73.2% last season in Minnesota), and he's adding 2.5 turnovers. That's why he's 149th over the last two weeks and 197th over the last month.

    I have him 96th, down from 86th, because I expect his percentages to rebound once the Hornets get healthier and he isn't carrying as much of the offense. The volume makes him an easier hold in points leagues, but fantasy managers have every right to be concerned about his numbers.

    #119548. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5954 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the latest signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    According to recent reports, title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Industry observers note that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    Industry observers note that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    According to recent reports, you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    It has been revealed that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    Sources indicate that it should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    In a recent development, city, in contrast to their opponents, highlighted a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where latest boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    Industry observers note that arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

    Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

    Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

    Referee Sam Barrott (Yorkshire).

    In a recent development, it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

    It has been revealed that I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we revealed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

    He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

    I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

    It has been revealed that the feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

    Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

    Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka.

    In a recent development, the players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

    Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7.

    It has been revealed that what happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

    We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

    It has been revealed that arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

    It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

    The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

    When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

    Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

    In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer aims remain up in the air for both camps.

    In a recent development, city appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

    Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

    In a recent development, although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the massive games is an area for improvement.

    The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) recently completed the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history, raising $81.3 billion -- beating the previous record set by SpaceX by $6.3 billion in June.
    • In a recent development, many investors were no doubt pleased with Anthropic's public debut, but individual retail investors aren't the only ones to benefit.
    • What's more, Alphabet has significant cloud computing and processor deals with Anthropic, further entangling the two companies' futures.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Chris Neiger – Nov 26, 2026 at 12:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) recently completed the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history, raising $81.3 billion -- beating the previous record set by SpaceX by $6.3 billion in June.

    In a recent development, many investors were no doubt pleased with Anthropic's public debut, but individual retail investors aren't the only ones to benefit. Alphabet (GOOGL -2.13%) (GOOG -2.02%) holds nearly 14% of Anthropic's shares, making it one of the largest shareholders in the artificial intelligence (AI) company.

    What's more, Alphabet has significant cloud computing and processor deals with Anthropic, further entangling the two companies' futures. Here's how Alphabet and its shareholders benefit from the recent Anthropic IPO.

    Starting in 2023, Alphabet made a series of investments in Anthropic over multiple funding rounds that eventually totalled about $33 billion. At the time of Anthropic's IPO, Alphabet held 13.7% of Anthropic's stock.

    That investment was a very wise move, considering that Anthropic's shares were priced at $83 at the IPO, making Alphabet's position worth about $149 billion. Of course, as Anthropic's shares rise and fall, the value of Alphabet's stake shifts.

    Industry observers note that holding Anthropic's shares boosts Alphabet's reported net income on paper each quarter (if Anthropic's returns go up), without generating actual cash. Alphabet could eventually sell some of its Anthropic shares to reinvest in the organization, but it's likely to hold on to them, or at least the bulk of them, for a while.

    Industry observers note that if Alphabet holds onto its stake, it could add significant unrealized gains to its reported income. When it sells some of its shares, it will directly benefit shareholders by providing fresh capital for growth or buybacks. So, even though Alphabet and Anthropic compete with their AI models, Alphabet shareholders will still benefit as Anthropic grows.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that anthropic said in its S-1 filing before going public that it had about $121 billion in spending committed to Google between April 2026 and July 2033. The good news for Alphabet was that Anthropic was locked into that spending "regardless of actual usage.".

    In a recent development, what's more, Anthropic also buys Google's tensor processing units (TPUs) for AI processing. The AI firm will reportedly spend $2.5 billion on Google's TPUs this year and up to $7.2 billion next year.

    Altogether, Anthropic is estimated to spend up to $200 billion on Google Cloud and TPUs over the next five years.

    Recent findings suggest that with Anthropic being a core Google Cloud and TPU customer, its financial stability is a good thing for Alphabet. Now that Anthropic has raised more than $81 billion from its IPO, the deals between the companies are essentially de-risked because it can use the proceeds to pay for some of its commitments.

    Recent findings suggest that and Anthropic could expand its deals with Alphabet in the future, as demand for its services increase. Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 47% to $17 billion, indicating that the manufacturer is already on the right growth trajectory.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that alphabet is positioning itself well in the AI era as the firm expands sales of its TPUs and grows its Google Cloud service. Morgan Stanley estimates that Google could generate $84 billion in graphics processing unit (GPU)-related sales next year alone. That would be an enormous opportunity for the company, considering that it only just began selling TPUs to customers earlier this year.

    What's more, the firm's Google Cloud revenue is rising fast and more than doubled in Q3 to $30.7 billion. The company ended the quarter with $561 billion in Google Cloud backlogs, 55% of which management notes will be fulfilled over the next 24 months.

    While Alphabet certainly benefits from its significant stake in Anthropic, I think the company's growth from Google Cloud and massive opportunity from selling TPUs make it a compelling AI stock on its own.

    And given that Alphabet's shares trade at just 15 times the company's trailing earnings -- compared to the tech sector average of about 24 -- the company's stock looks like a good buy right now.

Right now, looking back, overseas revenue was about 20% in 2024 and about 25% in 2025. This time, for the first 9 months of this year, it reached 31%. And second, what's the opportunity and how the strategy is evolving. I think 2 things are changing and where we operate and who we are, who we serve. On the market, we've gone from developed market into a developed one. The different growth risk profitability, and that's what makes them complementary.

    In a recent development, and on the customer side, we start with small online cash loans, and we are now moving towards better quality borrowers with larger loans and longer terms. And in Indonesia, our multi-finance license let us do offline Buy Now, Pay Later which was 31% of our Indonesia volume in Q3. In the Philippines, we are beyond -- going beyond cash loans with products like Buy Now, Pay Later card. The aim in both is higher customer lifetime value and better profitability. And the third, the challenges, I'd like to highlight 2. One is from regulation. In the developing markets, it can be changed swiftly. A rate cap change, for example, can slow growth in short term.

    Sources indicate that but we've been through this more than once last year, when Indonesia was affected. The Philippines helped offset it. The other is the macro side, both Indonesia and the Philippines, face inflation and currency pressure and the geopolitical environment adds to that. So we watch local conditions closely and adjust our pace in each market. On currency, we match local currency assets with local currency liability. So that limits the impact on our group. So overall, we are confident in Indonesia and the Philippines.

    Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Claire Ouyang from Goldman Sachs.

    Claire Ouyang: [Foreign Language] This is Claire Ouyang from Goldman Sachs. My question is about the asset quality for domestic business.     According to recent reports, jiayuan Xu: Thanks, Claire. I will take your questions. Yes, changes across the industry are starting to affect our existing loan book. That's the main reason credit risk has picked up. When funding tightened across the industry in July, some borrowers with high debt levels started to face liquidity pressure. So over time, it made it harder for them to keep up with payments on loans they had already taken out. And at the same time, changes in the collection environment made it harder to recover overdue payments. Together, these 2 factors put considerable pressure on asset quality across the industry in Q3. Let me put some numbers around it.

    Sources indicate that our day 1 delinquency rate rose 21% quarter-over-quarter from 5.26% in second quarter to 6.35% in the third quarter. Our 30-day collection rate fell from 89.4% to 85.5% and our CM2 flow rate rose from 0.56% to 0.92%. Our vintage estimate for loans originated in Q3 is 3.5%, up 80 basis points from the Q2 vintage. In terms of how we have responded, we started to tighten our risk controls in July and reduced our exposure further in August and September, shifting our focus from volume growth to asset quality. As we have mentioned, we have tightened underwriting for upcoming borrowers, refined how we manage existing borrowers, and strengthened our fraud controls.

    According to recent reports, we are also taking a close look at expected credit cost and profitability across the borrower segments and the loan portfolios. That really helped us adjust the pace of origination and give priority to loans with better risk-adjusted returns while keeping our overall exposure in check. But it takes time for those changes to show up across the portfolio. Our loans have an average tenure of 8 to 9 months. So it typically takes about 2 to 3 quarters for risk in the existing book to work its way out. We have already tightened underwriting on upcoming loans, but it will take time to see the full effect on the whole asset quality. So turning to the fourth quarter.

    In a recent development, our latest data reveals the CM2 flow rate, one of our early risk indicators reached a recent high at the end of September. And in October, it fell 6% from September. That was mainly due to a modest improvement in our 30-day collection rate. The collection rate is a very key part. So I'd like to add some more details. We have adjusted both our staffing and our strategy in response to our early pressure on recoveries. First, we have added staff to our in-house collections team and focus more resources on loans that are 1 to 30 days past due. In-house collectors now make up a large share of the staff handling these accounts up 19% from September.

    In a recent development, that helped us take a more active role in managing early delinquency. And second, we are expanding our use of AI in post loan management. We were already using AI for early-stage collections. Now we are also using it for accounts that have been overdue for longer. For those accounts, the monthly recovery rate with AI is almost 1.5x the rate third-party collection agencies achieved through phone calls. That indicates how AI can help improve collections efficiency. So take them together, these changes have strengthened our collection capacities and helped improve the recoveries. That helped during our 30-day collection rate a bit in October. That is the improvement is still recent.

    Industry observers note that it's still too early to call a turning point in credit risk, and we will need a bit more time to see where the improvement holds. So looking ahead, we expect risk to ease gradually and higher risk loans for early vintage result and as the mix of fresh loans continue to improve. The pace of recovery will still depend on the external environment. Yes, that's the key. We will keep a close eye on the risk indicators and adjust our origination volume accordingly with asset quality and profitability as our top priority.

Our buyback, we keep the pace flexible based on where our shares are trading, market liquidity, our cash position, and our overall capital need.     By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 26, 2026 at 1:08AM EST.

    In a recent development, need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected].

    It has been revealed that grupo Financiero Galicia (GGAL +3.90%) reported third-quarter results marked by a sequential compression in margins as the Argentine economy transitions toward lower inflation and reduced nominal interest rates. Management reported that while headline profitability fell 16% from the second quarter, underlying operational metrics improved through reduced loan loss provisions and lower administrative expenses. The company stated that the integration of HSBC Argentina is contributing to significant efficiency gains, with group expenses falling 36% year over year. The group maintained high liquidity and a strong capital position, which management stated provides strategic optionality to accelerate growth as credit demand recovers.

    Industry observers note that operator: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to Grupo Financiero Galicia Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. This conference is being recorded, and the replay will be available at the firm's website at gfgsa.com. [Operator Instructions] Some of the statements made during this conference call will be forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. federal securities laws and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed. Investors should be aware of events related to the macroeconomic scenario, the financial industry and other factors could cause results to differ materially from those expressed in the respective forward-looking statements. Now I will turn the conference over to Mr.

    Pablo Eduardo Firvida, Head of Investor Relations. You may begin your conference.

    Pablo Eduardo Firvida: Thank you. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining Grupo Galicia's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. I'm here with Gonzalo Fernández Covaro, our Chief Financial Officer. The third quarter was marked by lower inflation and lower interest rates. Therefore, returns on inflation-linked assets declined and the credit cycle showed signs of improvement. For Grupo Galicia, this produced a quarter with lower sequential profitability, but also with encouraging developments beneath the headline result. Credit indicators improved, provisions declined, expenses continue to fall, and our liquidity and capital position remained very strong. In our presentation today, we will first describe the operating environment and then the results of the group and its subsidiaries.

    In a recent development, unless otherwise indicated, all figures are stated in constant Argentine pesos as of September 30, 2026. The macroeconomic environment continued to combine fiscal discipline with softer economic activity. According to the Monthly Indicator of Economic Activity, MIEA, (sic) [ Monthly Estimator of Economic Activity, EMAE, ] the Argentine economy contracted 1.2% year-over-year in September, while edging up 1.1% month-over-month on a seasonally adjusted basis. Activity levels stood 2.4% below those recorded in December 2025. As of September 2026, the primary fiscal surplus reached 1.2% of GDP with total revenues declining 4.3% year-over-year in real terms and primary spending falling 2.3%. At the same time, inflation continued to moderate.

    Industry observers note that consumer prices increased 5.8% during the quarter compared with 6.8% in the second quarter. This was positive for purchasing power, planning and the long-term development of financial intermediation. In the short term, however, it also accelerated the decline in nominal interest rates and reduced the returns generated by CPI-linked assets. During the last 12 months, inflation reached 33.4% in September. The monetary base increased 0.9% in real terms during the third quarter and declined 16.4% in real terms compared with September 2025. The average exchange rate of the quarter was ARS 1,500 per dollar. And at the end of the quarter, the exchange rate reached ARS 1,517 per dollar, representing a 7.6% year-over-year depreciation.

    Industry observers note that dollar deposits remained dynamic, while in pesos, we see the transactional deposits declined year-over-year and time deposits gained share during the period. In terms of credit, the system data reflected the transition process of the macro. Real peso credit remained soft, while dollar lending continued to expand at a faster pace. In other words, the financial system moved toward a lower inflation environment, but the volume recovery was still uneven, with the volume of dollar intermediation becoming more relevant. Taken together, these trends frame our quarter. Lower inflation reduced the loss from the net monetary position, but asset yields declined faster than funding costs and volume growth is still lagging.

    Industry observers note that as a result, margins compressed before loan demand and transactional activity had fully recovered. Against this backdrop, Grupo Galicia generated net income of ARS 229 billion in the third quarter with an annualized ROE of 9.3% and an ROA of 1.7%. The result was 16% below the previous quarter, but represented a significant recovery from the loss recorded 1 year earlier. More importantly, profitability remained diversified. Banco Galicia contributed with ARS 134.9 billion, Galicia Asset Management with ARS 48.5 billion, Naranja X with ARS 29.3 billion, Galicia Seguros with ARS 11.4 billion and Galicia Securities with ARS 5.3 billion. This diversification is strategically relevant as it helps to stabilize the group's earnings capacity.

    It has been revealed that for the first 9 months of 2026, net income reached ARS 577.5 billion with an 8% ROE. The performance indicates that the group has moved beyond the losses recorded in 2025 and is rebuilding profitability on a more sustainable operating base. The decline in profitability from the second quarter was largely explained by the reduction in the group's financial margin, which fell to 14.4% as lower lending rates, lower CPI returns and fewer gains from security sales affected revenues. But this should be read together with positive developments. The cost of risk kept on decreasing from the peak recorded in December last year and expenses declined materially year-over-year, improving the efficiency ratio more than 20 percentage points.

    Banco Galicia, our largest subsidiary, is where the change in the earnings environment was most visible. Net income reached ARS 134.9 billion with a 7% ROE. The 19% sequential decline in profitability was primarily a consequence of margin compression, partially offset by the improvement in most of the lines related to expenses, in which our focus in efficiencies is showing results. During the quarter, average interest-earning assets increased 2% to ARS 32 trillion, but their average yield declined to 22.3% from 27.1%. Average interest-bearing liabilities increased 1%, while their cost fell to 9% from 10.1%.

    It has been revealed that funding costs moved in the right direction, but not as promptly as asset yields, which explains a significant part of the reduction in net interest income. Within the asset mix by currency, average peso loans grew 3%, foreign currency loans increased 9% and peso government securities declined 6%. This was a quarter of selective allocation with the bank reducing public sector exposure and prioritizing lending opportunities with an appropriate risk-adjusted return. Going to our interest-bearing liabilities, in the chart on the right, we can see the volume of those denominated in foreign currency, which increased by 6%. And on the left, that in pesos, they decreased 4%.

    According to recent reports, interest income reached ARS 1.7 trillion, declining 12% sequentially and 24% year-over-year as lending rates and CPI returns fell. Interest expenses reached ARS 586 billion, also decreasing quarter-over-quarter. When we compare the figures with the ones of the third quarter of the previous year, the reduction was significant, mainly due to the increase in the cost of funding associated to the volatility of the midterm elections that took place last year. Fee income amounted to ARS 317 billion and decreased 3% in real terms in the third quarter, with most of the sources of fees behaving similarly, while results from financial instruments returned to more normalized levels after the strong gains recorded in the second quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that FX results amounted to ARS 119 billion and increased 3% in the quarter, mainly due to the trading activity with our clients. The most encouraging development of the quarter was the change in credit trends. Loan loss provisions declined 12% sequentially to ARS 509 billion. The NPL ratio improved to 7.8% from 8.3%. Cost of risk fell to 8% from 9.3% and coverage increased to 96.1% from 92.8%. Fewer exposures migrated to Stage 3, deterioration in the retail portfolio slowed and nonaccrual financing declined. This suggests that the credit cycle began to stabilize during the quarter. We remain cautious as NPL levels are still above those recorded 1 year ago and improvement must be sustained over several quarters.

    Nevertheless, the direction of the trend is now positive. The actions taken in underwriting, collections, portfolio management and provisioning are beginning to translate into better asset quality metrics. This is crucial for the earnings outlook. As the cost of risk normalizes, a larger portion of operating income can translate into bottom line profitability even in a lower rate environment. The second major structural message is efficiency. Banco Galicia's expenses declined 10% quarter-over-quarter and 36% year-over-year to ARS 731 billion. Personnel expenses fell 15% sequentially. Administrative expenses declined 5% and other operating expenses were 10% lower. These reductions reflect the efficiency initiatives implemented throughout the year and the benefits of the integration with HSBC Argentina.

    Lower maintenance, IT, communications and administrative service costs demonstrate that the combined platform is beginning to operate with greater scale. The group's efficiency ratio was 39.4%. It increased sequentially because revenues compressed faster than expenses, but it improved by more than 20 percentage points compared with the third quarter of the previous year. Our objective is to continue simplifying the operating model while protecting customer experience, digital capabilities and the capacity to grow. Financing to the private sector totaled ARS 26 trillion and declined 3% sequentially, reflecting the softer level of demand and our selective approach to origination. Market share of financing to the private sector decreased 30 basis points to 14.7%.

    It has been revealed that deposits were stable at ARS 28.7 trillion, while private sector deposits market share increased 20 basis points to 14.5%. Peso-denominated deposits decreased 3%, while dollar deposits increased 3%. Time deposits in pesos increased 12%, while transactional deposits in pesos decreased 11%, negatively affecting the cost of funding. Liquidity remained high. Liquid assets represented 99.7% of transactional deposits and 56.1% of total deposits. Capitalization was equally strong with a total capital ratio of 25.7% and Tier 1 ratio of 25.6%. Computable capital exceeded the regulatory minimum by ARS 4.8 trillion. This buffer provides strategic optionality. They allow us to absorb volatility, protect the franchise and accelerate growth when demand returns and risk-adjusted spreads become more attractive.

    The quarter also demonstrated the value of Grupo Galicia diversified ecosystem. While Banco Galicia managed the pressure from lower rates, the other companies contributed with other sources of earnings and customer engagement. Together, these businesses expand the relationship with our customers beyond traditional banking. They allow the group to participate in payments, consumer finance, insurance, savings and capital markets, creating a broader and more balanced platform for growth. Naranja X generated net income of ARS 29 billion. Its profitability declined sequentially to an ROE of 9.3%, but credit indicators improved. The NPL ratio fell to 17.8% and cost of risk to 17.9%.

    The business continues to combine scale, digital engagement and financial inclusion while recalibrating growth to the current risk environment. Galicia Seguros reported net income of ARS 12 billion and a combined ratio of 92.8%, demonstrating the contribution of insurance to the group's fee and risk diversification strategy. Galicia Asset Management delivered net income of ARS 48 billion, while assets under management reached ARS 16.6 trillion. In a lower rate environment, the demand for savings and investment solution becomes increasingly notable, and our asset management franchise is well positioned to capture that opportunity. Now Gonzalo Fernández Covaro, our CFO, will make some additional remarks.

    In a recent development, gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Thank you, Pablo. Before taking your questions, I would like to add that the third quarter is part of a transition period. Lower inflation and lower rates are positive for Argentina and for the long-term development of financial intermediation, but they also changed the earnings equation faster than volumes could recover. This compressed margins and temporarily reduced profitability until volumes are recovered. At the same time, the underlying quality of our performance improved. Credit indicators began to turn, as we have said in calls -- in prior calls, provisions and cost of risk declined, expenses continue to fall and deposits remain stable and liquidity and capital stayed at very strong levels.

    These developments gives us the confidence that the direction of the business is the correct one. We are moving from an environment in which earnings were heavily influenced by inflation, high nominal rates and financial assets towards one in which sustainable profitability will be driven increasingly by customer activity, transaction volumes, fees, disciplined credit growth and an efficient operating platform. Our priorities for the coming quarters are therefore clear. We will actively manage the balance sheet to protect margins and grow our earning assets. We will maintain discipline in origination and collections to consolidate improvement in asset quality.

    In a recent development, we will continue capturing integration and efficiency benefits, and we will deploy capital selectively as attractive opportunities may emerge across our subsidiaries, Banco Galicia, Naranja X, Galicia Seguros and Galicia Asset Management. So Grupo Galicia enters next year with a leading franchise, a diversified ecosystem and substantial financial strength. The quarter showed that even as earnings mix changes, the foundations of the business are becoming stronger. So with that, we are ready to answer the questions that you may have.

    Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Ernesto Gabilondo from Bank of America.

    Ernesto María Gabilondo Márquez: My first question will be on your loan growth expectations for this next year?
