How should we think about the ROE for this year, next year? And how do you see the sustainable ROE in the next years?

    In a recent development, gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Thank you for the question. Well, regarding loan growth, I mean, we are seeing -- I mean, this year, maybe ending at around 5% growth. We are seeing some pickup in the peso volume in October. So we expect that if that continues, we can achieve a total loan growth of around 5% for the year in real terms. Talking about next year, we are seeing the growth -- asset growth between 5% and 10%, closer to 10%, I would say. So that's the expectations we have so far in terms of growth. In terms of returns on ROE, that was your second question.

    Industry observers note that I would say that for the fourth quarter, we expect the -- what we call the banking business, which is Galicia Asset Management and Galicia Securities to be between 8% and 9% ROE. Naranja X a bit lower than that. So that will put us as a total group for the full year 2026 in an ROE around 8%, I would say. Talking about next year, we need to take into account that next year is a year with the presidential election that will may bring political uncertainty. And at some point, it's not that easy to forecast, but we are seeing our returns in the low double-digit arena, I would say.

    So that's an improvement from the 8% on this year, ranging in the low double-digit range, I would say, for next year. We expect that, that will be like a step towards the 15% ROE that we are expecting for 2028. I mean what we expect is while we still have inflation accounting the ROE should be -- our target ROE is around 15%. So the building -- the step by step will be, let's say, low double digits next year, 15%, the year after '28, where we still are having inflation accounting. And by '29 and onwards, if with inflation accounting disappearing, if that happens, then our target is between 15% and 20%, closer -- more closer to 20%.

    That will be how we are seeing the longer-term profitability.

    Operator: The next question comes from Carlos Gomez-Lopez from HSBC.

    Industry observers note that carlos Gomez-Lopez: Gonzalo, Pablo, I wanted to follow up on what you mentioned now that October was a bit more -- there was a bit more activity. What are you seeing on the ground? I know there's a lot of concern that Argentina is not growing. Has there been any change, let's say, since the end of the third quarter? Have you -- are you starting to see any type of higher activity? And then when we look 3 to 5 years from now, I mean, you have this notable increase in the dollar business.

    Should we expect the group, the financial system as a whole to be more dollar-based or inflation-linked or go back to nominal pesos in the next, let's say, 3 to 5 years?

    According to recent reports, gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: I mean activity is not that what we have seen is more demand for pesos, but for working capital short term, discount of checks, short-term lending, nothing really switched significantly for longer-term projects. But yes, we have been seeing more demand for pesos that before it was mainly dollars. Interest rates in pesos have gone down somehow, and we have been seeing more demand from one side, from the commercial lending in the short term, but also we are starting to increase month after month our consumer lending, our personal lending after the bubble in NPLs that we put stricter origination policies. Of course, we continue with that.

    Sources indicate that but now we have been finding pools of customers that are within our risk appetite. And we have been growing month after month slowly, but consistently the personal loans portfolio. So that's also what we are seeing falling into the fourth quarter. No significant changes, but yes, slight changes. And in the commercial side, I would say, more towards demand of pesos, which has higher margins, as you know. And talking about the future, I would say, group or financial system considering where today, yes, we grew a lot dollars. This year, the dollars grew more than the peso.

    In a recent development, what we were expecting for next year to start also to change that also to have a better growth, even though dollars will continue growing, that the mix also tend to stop and somehow move towards the peso, considering also that next year with a presidential election, the entire financial system, we want to be more conservative in terms of dollar liquidity. So we expect dollar -- peso lending to grow more than dollar as a matter of the system having -- wanting to keep more dollar liquidity than this year.

    Recent findings suggest that but also considering the longer term, as you asked, I would say that we -- what we are seeing, and this is, of course, a matter that we can see different scenarios, but we see the financial system gradually going to inflation-linked for longer terms, like, for example, mortgages or car loans also. But going back to peso, if we -- Argentina continuing on the path of reducing inflation, having prudent macroeconomical policies will tend that the financial system go back to the peso. We always expect that the dollar will be a part of the financing, but with a smaller percentage than the one that we have seen in last year.

    Operator: The next question comes from Rafael Nobre from Safra.

    Industry observers note that rafael Nobre: My question goes to Naranja X. I see that asset quality improved, but credit portfolio decreased and deposits decreased as well. So I was just wondering how this limited risk appetite that you guys have been having is affecting client activity as a whole. And when we should expect some sort of normalization in terms of credit portfolio shrinking and then deposits shrinking as well? And if at any point in 2027, we could expect that this business could resume growth as well?

    Hernán García: Rafael, I'm here, Hernán García from Naranja X, I will take the answer. As you mentioned, the third quarter was -- resulted in a reduction in the portfolio with the same trend that we had during the second quarter, and it has to do with the risk appetite that we had. And as Gonzalo mentioned before, it also has to do with a soft demand from -- for credit -- consumer credit. We are starting to see some pickup in personal loans originations during the fourth quarter. But we expect, let's say, a more stable balance during the fourth quarter in comparison with the third quarter.

    We are not seeing or expecting a sharp change in the trends of credit demand at least for the next -- for the current quarter. But as I mentioned, there are different stories in considering the credit card portfolio and the personal loans portfolio. We are seeing more activity on the personal loans, and we expect that there will be a small rebound there. So for the whole year next year, obviously, we are close following the macro situation as a bank. We are expecting a slight rebound in personal loans balance. We are expecting 5% growth in real terms on a full year basis.

    According to recent reports, but in the case of the credit card portfolio, we are expecting a change of the trend for the second quarter of -- second half of the year. So as a whole, we're expecting, let's say, flattish behavior of the credit card portfolio and a growth in terms of personal loans.

    Operator: The next question comes from Diego Marquez from JPMorgan.

    In a recent development, diego Marquez Antonio: Just a quick question on margins. We saw assets repricing faster than deposits. So just trying to get a sense for the next couple of quarters if we should see lower deposit costs and margins stabilizing? And if I may, one more question, looking into 2027. So last year's elections, we saw some volatility in margins due to higher reserve requirements from the Central Bank. So just trying to get a sense of what you expect as we head into the 2027 elections and if we could see more volatility there.

    It has been revealed that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Thank you for the question. I mean -- talking about margins, I mean, we see margins like 2 components. One, as you stated, the asset repricing, but also the mix. And I think that this year, we grew more dollars than pesos and that, of course, has lower margins and impacted the total margin. And we also grew more corporate portfolio or commercial portfolio than consumer portfolio. Now I think the mix is 60-40. And that, of course, has lower margins, commercial lending than consumer lending. So that also affected the margin this year. And that's where you see asset rates dropping. It's also because of the mix rather than the individual products' asset rate reduction.

    I would say that for next year, I mean, if we consider group, I would say that this year, we're expecting to end the year at 16% margin, total year. And for next year, we are seeing something around 15%, a bit higher than 15%, 15.5%. So like holding -- even though the last quarter was lower, we expect that the increase in peso lending and also the increase in consumer lending via personal loans that has higher margins than commercial can hold at, let's say, 15%, 15%, around 15%, I would say, for the group.

    According to recent reports, for bank could be around 14%, the same 14.5%, 14%, the margin for next year for the bank, but also driven by -- which is, I would say, it's higher than the last quarter, but we are also expecting to change the mix to grow more dollar -- peso than dollar and to also [ recapture ] some of the lost volume in the consumer arena, mainly through personal lending, personal loans. Talking about volatility, I mean -- yes, I mean, we -- of course, in election year, it's impossible to predict what will happen.

    Industry observers note that I think that the government has -- or the Central Bank more than government has other tools to maintain stability rather than increase interest rates like the one that happened prior year that everyone understood that was not good for anyone. So we expect that with higher international reserves, higher liquid reserves, Central Bank has also other tools to try to keep stability in the FX other than interest rates. So we see lower chances to have the spike of interest rate than the one that we had last year. Of course, it's impossible to guarantee that, that won't happen, but we see lower chances.

    Operator: The next question comes from Nicolas Riva from Bank of America.

    It has been revealed that nicolas Riva: So I guess my question is, so looking at the GDP growth estimates for this year, of course, they have been revised downwards. And I think right now, they are about in the area of 1% growth for this year. Then for next year, most estimates are higher, right, between 2% and 3%. So it seems people are expecting some acceleration in the economy. And then you have shown in the slides that in your case, we have seen some improvement in the NPL ratio in the third quarter, I think about 50 basis points in the quarter.

    My question would be, maybe if you can comment on the downside risks that you are seeing to GDP growth next year, given that some of the deceleration in the economy seems to be driven by people anticipating a bit the election of next year. So given that next year, we are going to have the election, so perhaps more volatility because of that. Again, if you can discuss downside risk for growth next year?

    And then in the context of that, if in your case, that improvement we have seen in the NPL ratio in the third quarter, if you are seeing that as the beginning of further improvements in the NPL ratio or if you are seeing upside risks to NPLs next year?

    Sources indicate that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Thank you for the question. I mean regarding GDP growth, I mean, for next year, we have around 2%. We don't see 3%. So our estimations are closer 1.8% to 2%. Of course, that's something -- I mean we see downward risk, it all depends on the volatility and how the political uncertainty, first, how massive it is and how it affects the FX, the interest rates and all the variables of the economy, that will change and can bring the GDP growth even lower. But that is very difficult to predict.

    We need to see how the polls are, what the expectations on the -- if it's the current government or another government, which are the policies that they may implement. So I would say that the next year will be influenced by political uncertainty and how that political uncertainty impacts the economy variables like FX, like interest rates, that will have -- that may have a downside risk. For now, we are keeping the 2% -- around 2% arena for GDP growth. Talking about NPLs, I mean, we see -- even though GDP could grow lower than 2%, we see our NPLs to continue to improve.

    Of course, talking about the consumer arena where we have the spike in the past. In fact, we are expecting to end the year in the bank only at -- like at 7% and next year around 5.5%, between 5.5% and 6%. And that's with the portfolio we already have and the portfolio we are originating month after month in the last couple of months because remember that we -- in order to increase or to improve the credit quality, we cut some -- or put more tough the origination policy. So there are sectors we stop lending to.

    It's not that we -- so as we are lending to sectors that are better, we expect those to continue with the same payment capability. So we are expecting to see that in the bank and in group also to reduce to end maybe the year with NPLs 8.5%, 8.8% and at the end of the year, next year around 7.8%, 7.5%. So we expect to continue to see -- in fact, for next year, we are seeing also our cost of risk reducing by like 200 basis points from this year because we are confident that the portfolio will continue improving regardless what happened with the GDP.

    Of course, that if the GDP is too bad, then well, we -- our growth in terms of lending could be affected. But the loans that we already granted and the ones that we are continuing to grant in the next 3, 4 months, we are confident that we are going to provide a relief in terms of NPLs and cost of risk.

    Operator: The next question comes from Pedro from Latin Securities.

    Pedro Offenhenden: I wanted to ask on write-offs, which more than tripled in Banco Galicia and Naranja X. Maybe what drove that increase and if we should expect this level of write-offs in the following quarters? And if I may add a follow-up. When I look at the dollar loan book, I saw it was flat, but the export prefinancing grew about 30% in real terms. So I wanted to ask what line offset the prefinancing exports.

    Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: I mean, talking about write-off, yes, you saw we expect this to be the level of write-off going forward. I mean last quarter, we made some changes where we increased -- we saw that in order to collect the loans, we took more than the 270 days that we have as a policy, so we increased it to 365, which is more consistent with the period that we are getting to customers and what's going on with the increase in NPLs. So that's why you saw a reduction maybe in the second quarter, but the third quarter now that's already gone.

    So this is the level of write-off from now, and they can grow because we are going to grow portfolio, but this is the level you will see in the next month. And the other question was? I don't remember.

    Pablo Eduardo Firvida: The FX, the trade lines in dollars were growing, which one was offsetting that other short-term?

    Industry observers note that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes. I mean we grew a lot -- I mean, it's what the demand we saw in dollar terms was more exporters. At the beginning, we have been having other short terms to other exporters, but that's not a particular industry or sector that we saw product. We have seen some short-term lines in dollars to other customers and the trade finance increased, and that was the compensation. But nothing, I would say, in particular, we see a drop in any particular product.

    Operator: [Operator Instructions] The next question comes from Agustin Pacheco from Banco Mariva.

    Recent findings suggest that agustin Pacheco: Looking ahead to 2027, how do you expect net interest margin to evolve as interest rate and inflation continue to normalize? Do you expect margins to recover from current levels or remain under pressure over the coming quarters?

    Recent findings suggest that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: I would say that margin 2027, will -- I mean, for example, will be a bit lower than this than the full year, but a bit higher than the last quarter, mainly because what I noted before that we are -- we believe that next year we'll have a recovery of the consumer lending that has higher margins, a different mix in products, I would say. We will continue growing commercial lending, but also to do a catch up in the peso lending and the mix to increase peso versus dollar, also considering that next year is an election year, we want to have more liquidity in dollars and that will also drive that equation.

    According to recent reports, and also to have a higher participation in the consumer lending via personal loans that has a higher margin. So that's what we are expecting as a group around, I would say, 15.5%, let's say, for next year, between around 15% or 15.5% and the bank 14%, 14.5% arena, at the level of the margin, which is higher than the fourth or the third quarter, but lower than the full year because the first 2 quarters, remember, were higher. Of course, we need to also see what will happen with government bonds and yields on that arena and possibilities of sales of bonds that also affect margins.

    But in our forecast, it's just the plain intermediation and the portfolio -- the accrual of the portfolio of bonds that we already have.

    Operator: The next question is from Tiago Pinho from Bradesco BBI.

    Tiago Pinho: So I have a question regarding provisions and NPLs. So this quarter, provisions outpaced by a lot NPL formation. When we look at the ratio, probably we are seeing that Banco Galicia is being a lot more prudent on credit risk. And I just wanted to understand if there is some upside risk that provisions should go down in the upcoming quarters as NPLs start to fall?

    Recent findings suggest that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes. I mean, yes, as you see, our reserve coverage has been also going up and closer to the 100% where we want to be. I mean, as we start growing again, you start to see reserve formation and the provisions and it's what we are seeing. I would say that we -- I don't see us being much far away from the 100% we are achieving. We believe that by year-end, we may be at 100% reserve coverage. So I really don't see a big opportunity for that to -- for that reserve coverage to go down, but it's because mainly new loans coming into the portfolio that, of course, generate new reserves.

    It has been revealed that those reserves of the newly introduced portfolio are still a bit higher than the performance that those guys will have because, as you know, like IFRS 9 and how the reserve model works, you still need to use the experience of the last portfolios, even though you can do some adjustments to that. But with time, of course, that the reserve provisions -- the new reserve provisions, we are going to go lower and lower as the portfolios continue to evolve. But I would say that the first months of next year or the first half, we'll still be similar levels because still the models require that level of provisioning.

    In a recent development, tiago Pinho: Okay. Super clear. What about 2027? Can we expect maybe recomposed reserves by 110%, maybe even higher?

    Sources indicate that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: You're talking about coverage? Yes. I mean I would say that 110% is prudent or it seems right. And as I stated, we are expecting cost of risk to go down next year, like a couple of hundred basis points. So that will -- even though that you will see a reduction in P&L impact over -- talking about reserves, we see cost of risk going down.

    Operator: The next question comes from Federico Cabelli from AdCap.

    Federico Cabelli: So considering your shares are presently trading around 0.7x price to book value, are you considering a share buyback program soon?

    Sources indicate that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: We have a technical problem with buyback that the one that needs to do the buyback is the group because it's the one that issued the shares and the group doesn't have liquidity or has very small liquidity because it's a holding manufacturer. So what we are thinking is that next year -- in next dividend season, because remember that dividends needs to be approved by Central Bank. It's not that I can pay dividends whenever I want. I need to wait for the regulations to be issued and then pay dividends on the retained earnings or on the results of the year before.

    According to recent reports, so what we are thinking is that we will analyze if we want to leave some of the dividends at group level to face fresh opportunities of low prices for share buybacks. Today, we have that constraint that the holding company doesn't have much liquidity, and we cannot pay dividends at this point because of regulations. So we don't have a cash, I would say.

    Operator: The next question comes from Lisandro Lloveras from One618.

    It has been revealed that lisandro Lloveras: I have a question regarding loans and deposits. I'm sorry if you have already commented before, but I did not hear. Do you have guidance for 2027 loans and deposit growth?

    Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes. I mean talking about loan growth, we are talking about, I mentioned, between 5% and 10%, closer to 10% is that what we see in real terms and deposits on the same level between 5% and 10%, somewhat closer to 10%. That's what we are seeing for next year.

    Lisandro Lloveras: And regarding cost of risk, is it possible we would see cost of risk in the group in the level of 7% or 8%, or is it too optimistic?

    Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: At group level, I would say that 7% is optimistic. We see more around 8%, 8.5%.

    Operator: The next question comes from Carlos Gomez from HSBC.

    Sources indicate that carlos Gomez-Lopez: A follow-up question. You had a large OCI. I imagine that is the adjustment for your available-for-sale portfolio. What should we expect for that for the next quarter? And what is your strategy going forward in the next year or 2 years? Will you continue to have your securities mostly in available-for-sale? Second question, your cost, I mean, it's very impressive what you have done with the cost base. I calculate you have reduced your staffing levels by 23% over the last 2 years. Are we at the bottom? Or do you still need to reduce the cost base or the personnel further?

    It has been revealed that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Thank you, Carlos. Regarding OCI, yes, I think in the last couple of days, I would say, the market has been hit significantly. So far, I would say that we may be like ARS 300 billion negative OCI, I think, that at the end of September, we were like 100 or something, but I don't have the number in my head, I have the last one. But of course, that's -- as you know, it's included in the capital ratio because that's included in the equity. I mean, we expect -- I mean, of course, that the credit continue to -- or start to have more demand, then, of course, that the investments in bonds will be reduced accordingly.

    Sources indicate that but yes, I would say that something we review every time. But mostly, we expect that our investments, as we don't have them as a trading to buy 1 day and sell in 2 days, when we buy securities because we see a good yield and that we want to have it accrued in our balance sheet until we see any other opportunity, our expectation will be that mostly will continue to be OCI -- so same what we are doing this year. Talking about head count, I mean, the major part, as you mentioned, was done, that was mainly due to the HSBC acquisition.

    As you know, we are already the same or a bit lower amount of head count than before the acquisition. And we have also a lower amount of branches than before the acquisition. So we already integrated the balance sheet with the same or less amount of heads on branches that the one that Galicia has before acquiring HSBC. We continue to do things here and there. I mean if you see this quarter, we may -- we reduced almost 100 or between 70 and 100 heads. So we continue with efficiency programs, nothing with the size so far, and we continue analyzing our subsidiaries also to see how they are behaving, and we may see opportunities in the future.

    It has been revealed that for now, we are continuing with like business-as-usual efficiency programs, but we are analyzing every opportunity that we may have, and we may see something to implement in the future. But so far, I would say the business usual, but you will see a continued reduction in the head count arena.

    Pablo Eduardo Firvida: I would like to add one thing, Gonzalo. In the OCI, the bonds available-for-sale, most of them are in pesos, either adjusted by CPI or dual bonds and with very short-term maturity on average, I would say, 1.5 years, something like that.

    Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes, that's a good point, Pablo. On dollars, we have very small exposure. It's all peso bonds with very good yields, inflation plus 7%, 8% or TAMAR plus something high. So -- but, yes.

    Operator: The next question comes from Martin Argento from Delta Asset Management.

    Martin Argento: Sorry, do you hear me?

    Martin Argento: I have 2 quick questions. Yes. First, Asset Management made almost 1/4 of the group's profit. So I think how much of this is recurring fees and which is the impact you expect to see in this segment with the new Merval ETF? We can see similar figures for the following quarters. And on the other hand, what I see in other reports of other banks that small and medium companies delinquency is going up. So how do you see that going forward? And if you will be -- see, I don't know, an impact in Galicia NPLs for the following quarters?

    Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes. Regarding Asset Management, yes, it has been an vital part of our portfolio and our income. As you stated, we manage -- we call this segment the banking business, which is bank asset management and Galicia Securities for us is one unit, economic unit and one business. So we never see bank ROE by itself, even though here in the press release, we put it by itself. We look at it as the banking business ROE, then the fintech business, which is Naranja X and then the insurance business, which is what insurance firm, of course. But -- so for us, asset management is part of the banking business because it's the same customer, same everything.

    Sources indicate that we -- yes, the new ETF, I think it's a good thing for the market, but we don't expect that to -- we expect asset management to continue with a very good performance and the customers to continue to invest in our funds. So we don't see any impact on the contrary. So we expect asset management to -- and the funds to continue to be an notable part of our income. Today, of course, as you know, the money market is the star. But as Argentina continue in a stabilization path, then other funds more sophisticated should start picking up.

    It has been revealed that so that's what we have been preparing for to have also other offers when the money market, the plain vanilla money market lose attractiveness, then what the other ones can bring. So we continue to expect to continue to keep and gain market share and continue to be one of the leading asset managers in the country and continue to have a good net income. And the other question talking about SMEs, small and medium enterprises, NPLs. I mean, it's true that NPLs for SMEs started after the consumer NPLs. For us, it's a small portfolio. So even though we saw an increase in NPLs, you don't see that in the numbers because it's -- the impact is not big.

    Sources indicate that we are starting to see some kind of stabilization, not reduction so far, stabilization. And by next year, we expect that those NPLs started to improve. But in the numbers of the bank, they are no material, so they don't move the needle in terms of NPLs as a whole.

    Operator: We have another question from Ernesto Gabilondo from Bank of America.

    Ernesto María Gabilondo Márquez: I have a question on competition. Mercado Pago seems to become a more relevant player in Argentina, especially after it obtains the banking license. So just wanted to hear from you what are the risks or concerns that you see once Mercado Pago starts operations?

    Industry observers note that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: I mean we take Mercado Pago very seriously as an notable competitor before getting banking licenses and that will be after that. Of course, that will be -- I mean, on one hand, I think it's good because we are going to be all with the same regulations and the same taxes and everything similar. So that helps to put the playing field even. But of course, they will be able to do things that they cannot do now. So we take them serious as well we are implementing a lot of new value proposition.

    Industry observers note that we are -- we think that our right to win is also in the middle and middle upper segments that demands more sophisticated products and it's where we are also targeting latest offers for customers around Éminent. And where we see that, again, we have more the right to win than a fintech because of the complexity of the products we can offer. We are also redesigning all our investment platform for next year for customers to give more value added on top of what a digital wallet can offer. With time, they will catch up for sure, and will be another competitor, and we are happy to compete.

    Recent findings suggest that but we believe that, again, we have high-level technology in terms of our app. We have also an Naranja X that competes with Mercado Pago directly with same products. And that's the way we have been competing and will continue. We expect also that the Argentina financial system to continue to grow. And as today, I think we are at 12% of loan to GDP that continue to grow, that also will give room for everyone to compete and to grow.

    Operator: The question-and-answer session is over. We would like to hand the floor back to Pablo Eduardo Firvida for the company's final remarks.

    Industry observers note that pablo Eduardo Firvida: Okay. Thank you all for joining this call. And well, I hope you have a great day and Happy Thanksgiving for the ones in the Northern Hemisphere. Bye-bye.

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 1:43AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Genpact ›.

    In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, Genpact (G +3.12%) confirmed that full-year revenue growth will reach at least 7% as its automated artificial intelligence strategy, called Agentic Operations, takes hold. For long-term investors, the corporate pivot shifts the business away from labor-heavy services toward recurring software-like revenue streams.

    Industry observers note that structural margin gains and rapid technology adoption position the enterprise for compounding long-term returns. Three things management remarked on the call stand out.

    The company is accelerating its transition into Agentic Operations, expanding its total addressable market (TAM) -- the total revenue opportunity available -- and locking in higher-margin recurring contracts.

    By shifting client contracts away from full-time equivalent, or FTE, labor billing toward outcome-based software arrangements, gross margin expanded to 36.9%.

    Genpact is deliberately dropping legacy accounts that do not align with its technology strategy, creating a short-term two-percentage-point growth drag to secure long-term profitability.

    Demand for automated enterprise workflows is expanding, lifting gross margin and building long-term contract backlog. Deep process intelligence and proprietary software assets provide structural advantages over legacy outsourcing peers. Management is watching execution speed and client rotation into recurring digital agreements.

    Long-term performance depends on converting contract wins into durable recurring revenue while capturing market share across major global clients.

    According to recent reports, when our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 785%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 200% for the S&P 500.

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:34AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    According to recent reports, nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) stock has gotten slammed over the past few weeks. It all started with co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang resigning from his position. While he's back in the CEO role, news of investigations into Nvidia's export controls are also weighing down the stock.

    When the outlook is uncertain, that's normally the best time to buy stocks, as fear controls the market rather than logic. When you look at the growth Nvidia is expected to deliver, I think the stock is an absolute buy, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see it rise to $660 per share by 2028.

    In a recent development, that's a huge gain from today's levels, but how is that possible? Let's take a look.

    In a recent development, there is no doubt that Huang built an incredible organization, and he was an integral part of it. With him back in his role, the company he built remains intact. However, he's not the only one in the building. Nvidia has built a tech-centered company that has given it a huge advantage in the AI realm. Nvidia's products are better than the competition and practically sell themselves.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Sources indicate that investors should keep an eye on the future, as product development is a major reason why Nvidia has created a huge lead. Huang returning to the CEO role is major news for Nvidia's product development. Huang has made several tough decisions over the years as to how to shift product development, and his vision and technical knowledge are unparalleled in the industry. Nvidia’s stock skyrocketed 31% on the day he was reinstated, underscoring this.

    There will certainly be huge growth in the field, as several AI hyperscalers anticipate spending more in 2027, building on an already record-breaking 2026. AI demand is real, and Nvidia can produce enough computing units to meet demand. In fact, Nvidia estimates revenue will grow at a 75% pace in its next fiscal year. Some companies don't forecast that far into the future because visibility that far out is hard to achieve. But with the industry in a supply-constrained state, it's easier for Nvidia to estimate how many chips it will be able to sell.

    Nvidia looks set to have another year of solid growth in 2028, although a 75% clip again likely won't be in the cards.

    So, where will that put the stock price by then?

    In a recent development, thanks to the turmoil surrounding the leadership transition, Nvidia's stock now trades at a dirt cheap 16.6 times trailing earnings. I don't think that's a reasonable price for the stock to trade at, as I think a 30x valuation is far more reasonable, given its market position and growth prospects.

    Wall Street analysts estimate Nvidia will generate around $424 billion in its next fiscal year. Assuming management’s 75% growth rate is accurate, that brings its total to $742 billion. Over the past 12 months, Nvidia's profit margin has eclipsed 60%, but I'll set it at 60% to bake in a bit of conservatism. That would mean Nvidia will generate around $445 billion in profits.

    Industry observers note that if we assume Nvidia can grow at an additional 20% year-over-year pace in 2028 (which is Nvidia’s fiscal 2029), that would bring its profit total to $534 billion. At a 30x earnings valuation, Nvidia’s market cap would be $16 trillion, or a $660 per-share stock price.

    That's a huge gain from today's levels, and it requires Nvidia to return to a reasonable valuation and meet projections. If it can do that, Nvidia's stock is a generational buy at today's price tag.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the fresh Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions.
    • “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City.
    • It has been revealed that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the fresh Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

    “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

    It has been revealed that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

    Industry observers note that as it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    Sources indicate that there was also another promising performance by latest signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

    “They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

    Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

    It has been revealed that “Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they indicated it,” Lampard noted. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

    "They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

    Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he stated, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

    According to recent reports, if that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

    In a recent development, the energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment newly introduced signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

    The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

    Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their newly introduced club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

    Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the upcoming £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    It has been revealed that odegaard demonstrated in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

    In a recent development, "It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx.

    According to recent reports, from there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

    It has been revealed that "How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I.

    "I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE.

    In a recent development, it’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

    FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J.

    In a recent development, there will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

    Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

    Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

    Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

    Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

    Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

    Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

    Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

    Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

    Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

    Recent findings suggest that tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

    The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

    Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

    Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

    The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a substantial deflection and flies out for a corner.

    According to recent reports, from a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

    Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

    According to recent reports, it’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

    Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

    White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

    It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6.

    Sources indicate that odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

    According to recent reports, we are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

    It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

    It has been revealed that arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

    Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

    There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

    It has been revealed that the ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

    Recent findings suggest that tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

    Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

    Sources indicate that at the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

    It has been revealed that coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

    Recent findings suggest that christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

    Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

    Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

    In a recent development, rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    According to recent reports, arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

    Recent findings suggest that coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

    Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

    The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

    Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

    Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

    Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

    Recent findings suggest that following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

    Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

    Sources indicate that the atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

    Fresh Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

    The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

    Sources indicate that coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

    Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The upcoming signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

    With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

    Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

    Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

    Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

    Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

    It has been revealed that speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of upcoming stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”.

    Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so key to this club over the last seven years.

    Industry observers note that martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

    In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

    If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

    The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

    Odegaard comes into the upcoming Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

    Recent findings suggest that last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

    Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

    Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

    "Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the fresh Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T.

    After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

    Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

    "I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W.

    According to recent reports, on Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a newly introduced chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

    He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

    Industry observers note that his return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he noted.

    “The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”.

    Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s upcoming manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

    Recent findings suggest that riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

    The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

    It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

    Recent findings suggest that "I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w.

    New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

    Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

    It has been revealed that your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF.

    As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

    Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

    🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA.

    To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

    The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

    Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

    “Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”.

    Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

    Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy.

    Sources indicate that good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a latest season. A classic Arteta-ism.

    Sources indicate that the assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without fresh £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

    Meanwhile, Arteta has stated he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

    “In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta remarked. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”.

    Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

    “We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”.

    According to recent reports, this is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

    Full team news as and when we get it.

    With stocks mounting a comeback Wednesday, options trading across a few key volatility products suggests significant swings in stocks may dampen in the near term.

    According to recent reports, more than 80,000 options traded on the Barclays S&P 500 VIX Short Term Futures ETN (VXX), almost three times the 30-day average, with more puts trading than calls, according to LiveVol data. The fund aims to track the moves in Cboe's VIX Index, which surged to 35 early Wednesday but slipped to below 28 as the S&P 500 rallied to within 25 basis points of unchanged.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, options volume on VIX itself was 50% above average, with an even more distinctive bias towards puts, suggesting traders see stocks firming, or at least, the size of the market's moves shrinking. Of the 850,000 options traded on VIX, more than 515,000 were puts, with twice as many puts likely initiated by buyers than calls, Cboe data show.

    #119498. Saudi national in OpenAI bugging case is out on bond after DOJ tries to block release

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (589 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Saudi national in OpenAI bugging case is out on bond after DOJ tries to block release

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Abdulrahman Alfozan, the Saudi national accused of bugging an executive conference room at OpenAI's headquarters, has been released from custody, his attorney told CNBC on Wednesday.
    • The confirmation of Alfozan's release came a day after a federal judge in San Francisco remarked the defendant would be allowed out of jail on a $1 million bond, despite prosecutors' warnings that he posed a serious flight risk.
    • Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, is expected to be fitted with an ankle monitor, his attorney, David Rizk, previously told CNBC.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Abdulrahman Alfozan, the Saudi national accused of bugging an executive conference room at OpenAI's headquarters, has been released from custody, his attorney told CNBC on Wednesday.

    The confirmation of Alfozan's release came a day after a federal judge in San Francisco remarked the defendant would be allowed out of jail on a $1 million bond, despite prosecutors' warnings that he posed a serious flight risk.

    Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, is expected to be fitted with an ankle monitor, his attorney, David Rizk, previously told CNBC.

    Sources indicate that alfozan was scheduled to be released from detention Wednesday morning at 8 a.m. PT. Shortly before that deadline, U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian of the Northern District of California urged the court to maintain Alfozan's detention pending trial, "given the significant risk that the defendant will flee to Saudi Arabia if he is released from custody.".

    In a recent development, in an order posted on the case docket later Wednesday, Judge Vince Chhabria stated the court only learned of the government's last-minute bid to block Alfozan's release after he had already been let out.The government's motion "is therefore denied as moot," Chhabria's order stated. The judge set a hearing for Dec. 3 on the bid to revoke the magistrate judge's order releasing Alfozan.

    Pointing to Alfozan's "ample resources, significant family and professional ties to Saudi Arabia, and few remaining ties to the United States," Missakian had argued in a court filing that the release conditions imposed by Magistrate Judge Alex Tse "are insufficient to safeguard the defendant's appearance for future proceedings in this case.".

    Alfozan "presents a serious risk of flight that no set of release conditions can reasonably mitigate," Missakian wrote.

    Recent findings suggest that his office sought to pause the magistrate judge's release order until a ruling on a motion to revoke it. The Department of Justice did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Alfozan's release.

    Tse in a court hearing Tuesday ruled in favor of Rizk's motion for his client's release, which said prosecutors have admitted finding "no latest evidence to support the theory that Mr. Alfozan was stealing trade secrets, or to support the speculation that he was acting as an unregistered foreign agent for Saudi Arabia.".

    In a text message to CNBC after that hearing, Rizk said, "We are simply grateful that the Court made the right decision to release Mr. Alfozan and now we look forward to defending the case.".

    But Missakian's filing Wednesday morning pushed back, saying "the government's investigation of this seven-week-old case is ongoing.".

    Prosecutors have so far found "hundreds of audio files" on Alfozan's personal computer, "including dozens of recordings of meetings or conversations that occurred at OpenAI throughout September 2026, at least one of which involved representatives of a foreign government and many of which involved discussions of what may be trade secrets," according to the filing.

    "To be sure, what the defendant did or intended to do with those audio files remains under investigation, but the absence of that evidence at this point has no bearing" on whether Alfozan is a flight risk, Missakian argued.

    Alfozan was arrested Oct. 9 and is accused of concealing a recording device in the artificial intelligence manufacturer's conference room to secretly record discussions. The device was found in a USB port in a television in the room on Sept. 30, prosecutors have remarked.

    According to recent reports, jury selection for Alfozan's trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 20.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to this report.

    Crypto talent will return ‘when AI implodes,’ Arthur Hayes says

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Startup talent that has concentrated in artificial intelligence will return to the crypto industry "when AI implodes," according to Arthur Hayes, chief investment officer at Maelstrom Fund.
    • "A lot of talent has gone into the AI space, so I definitely think there'll be a resurgence in good founder talent coming back to crypto," Hayes said in an online interview with CNBC on Tuesday.
    • He added that some founders may also return once they "recognize" that their products could eventually be "usurped by Anthropic or OpenAI.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Startup talent that has concentrated in artificial intelligence will return to the crypto industry "when AI implodes," according to Arthur Hayes, chief investment officer at Maelstrom Fund.

    "A lot of talent has gone into the AI space, so I definitely think there'll be a resurgence in good founder talent coming back to crypto," Hayes said in an online interview with CNBC on Tuesday.

    He added that some founders may also return once they "recognize" that their products could eventually be "usurped by Anthropic or OpenAI.".

    The scale and capabilities of the largest frontier AI labs have made it difficult to "build a real AI business," Hayes mentioned, arguing that "most" founders simply "raise a bunch of money and then light it on fire.".

    He expects the AI trade to face "serious headwinds" in the second half of 2027, when leading labs begin confronting sizable bills tied to compute leases and other non-cancelable commitments.

    Anthropic expects about $451.6 billion in compute and infrastructure obligations through the end of 2030, with roughly $70.7 billion due by the end of September 2027, according to its prospectus.

    "Do they have the money? We're going to find out," Hayes said.

    Sources indicate that broader enthusiasm around the AI trade has also cooled amid questions about future infrastructure spending. Even exuberance from Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO on Monday proved short-lived, with the shares falling 5.9% on Tuesday and Anthropic dropping below its IPO price four days after its debut.

    Recent findings suggest that the co-founder of now-shuttered crypto exchange BitMEX also thinks bitcoin could test $50,000 if the Nasdaq continues to fall. The cryptocurrency has shown little sign of recovery after dropping as low as $55,142.16 on Saturday — its lowest level since July.

    Bitcoin hit an all-time high of $126,279.63 in October last year and traded as high as $97,915.90 in January this year.

    It has now fallen for seven straight weeks — only the third such streak in its history — with crypto exchange Bitfinex attributing the weakness to equity-market sentiment rather than interest-rate expectations.

    Hayes said he would like to see bitcoin rebound from around $55,000 even as the Nasdaq continues to fall. That divergence, he said, would suggest markets were shifting from a broad sell-off toward pricing in a "reflation" scenario, with the Federal Reserve eventually providing more liquidity.

    Neither bitcoin nor gold has yet decoupled from the Nasdaq, with Hayes describing the current market moves as a "correlation-led liquidation.".

    "Stuff goes down, you sell crypto first because it's easy, and then you sell everything else," he noted.

    Once that pattern changes, Hayes mentioned he would be interested in owning Zcash, which he described as a "high beta bitcoin" with a greater focus on privacy, as well as ENA, the token of Ethereum-based platform Ethena.

    Industry observers note that hayes mentioned a bitcoin rally could push up funding rates and futures-basis returns, increasing the income Ethena earns from its hedged crypto positions. That could make USDe, Ethena's synthetic dollar, more attractive and expand its circulation, he said, adding that he expects the ENA token to rise materially.

    "Those are the two things that I'm keeping an eye on, and when I'm ready to pull the trigger on buying risk again, those will be the things we buy a lot of," Hayes stated.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their major-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    It has been revealed that “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” mentioned head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    In a recent development, A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the newly introduced season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a major cheer from the home fans.

    Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    It has been revealed that he lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    Sources indicate that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal.
